title: Archimedean Substrate Period, Borromean Ratio, and Inhomogeneous Lepton-Resolvent Evaluation ($\mathcal{L}_1$)
html:
Prior-art reduction. Evaluation of the hyperbolic volume of the figure-eight complement S^3 \setminus 4_1 as two regular ideal tetrahedra via the Clausen dilogarithm \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 6\,\Lambda(\pi/3) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) follows Bruno Martelli [martelli2016, Thm. 13.1.3, Cor. 13.1.4], while empirical mass-ratio comparisons use CODATA-2022 (Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga [codata2022]) (Mass integrand, Uniqueness of the mass identity, Unified mass formula, Borromean Markov trace).

  • Input: Physical calibration observables (m_e, \mathfrak{D}_\beta, m_\pi) (Three-calibration discipline), supplying the leptonic energy unit m_e, the real substrate modulus q_0 > 1 (\hbar_{q_0} = 1 - q_0^{-1}) pinned by \mathfrak{D}_\beta via either the primary proton-to-electron ratio m_{\mathfrak{p}}/m_e or the comparison muon-to-electron ratio m_\mu/m_e, and the orthogonal meson scale m_\pi.
  • Output: Substrate parameters (q_0^{(p)}, q_0^{(\mu)}), dimensionless ratios m_\mu/m_e and m_{\mathfrak{p}}/m_e, inhomogeneous loop-resolvent shift between the two anchor arms, and intranucleon electromagnetic splitting contribution at 80 decimal places.
  • QOU delta (Borromean ratio root and inhomogeneous 4_1 loop resolvent): Evaluate the exact Borromean Markov trace |\tau_q(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})| = (4 + h^2 - 3h^4 - h^6)/(h^2 + 4) (h = q - q^{-1}, under z = q^3/(q^2+1)) and assemble
  F_{\mathrm{Bor}}(q) \;=\; \frac{|\tau_q(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})| \cdot [3]_q!}{q^3},
  \qquad
  \Phi_p(q) \;=\; 2\,\frac{\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)}{\hbar_q^2}\,F_{\mathrm{Bor}}(q) - 12,

where \dim V_{(2,1)} = 2, |S_3| = 6, and the factor q^{-3} in F_{\mathrm{Bor}}(q) is an asserted writhe-normalization convention of the model rather than a derived identity. Solving \Phi_p(q_0^{(p)}) = m_{\mathfrak{p}}/m_e by Newton iteration on the analytic Clausen/rational graph yields q_0^{(p)}, while \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_{q_0^{(\mu)}}^2 = m_\mu/m_e yields q_0^{(\mu)}. Because the homogeneous trace ratio \tau_e(q)/\hbar_q^2 > 6 for all q > 1, reconciling the toroidal Hopf electron (\mathrm{Vol} = 0) with the hyperbolic 4_1 muon (\mathrm{Vol}(4_1) > 0) evaluates the inhomogeneous Borel-resummed loop resolvent W(X; q) = W_{\mathrm{alg}}(X; q) + \hbar_q^{-2}\mathrm{Vol}(X)(1 + c_{\mathrm{tors}}(X)\hbar_q + c_2(X)\hbar_q^2), separating the zero-volume algebraic contact branch (\tau_{4_1}(q) = (h^4 + 3h^2 + 1)/(q + q^{-1})^2) from the 4_1 Riley--Reidemeister torsion saddle branch without auxiliary fitted loop factors.

  • Complexity and precision: \mathcal{O}(D \log D) bit complexity at D = 80 decimal digits via rapid Clausen series acceleration and quadratic Newton refinement with truncation bound \le 10^{-60}.
